title: Cabinet Approves Rs 62,370 Crore Fertiliser Subsidy for Rabi Season, DAP Price Held
excerpt: The Union Cabinet has approved Nutrient Based Subsidy rates for phosphatic and potassic fertilisers for Rabi 2026-27 with a tentative outlay of Rs 62,370.02 crore, up nearly 64% on the previous Rabi season, while holding the retail price of a 50 kg DAP bag at Rs 1,350.
body:
• The Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) rates on phosphatic and potassic (P&K) fertilisers for Rabi 2026-27, covering October 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
  • The tentative budget requirement is Rs 62,370.02 crore, about 64% higher than the Rs 37,952.29 crore for Rabi 2025-26 — an increase of Rs 24,417.73 crore.
  • The subsidy covers 28 grades of P&K fertilisers, including DAP and NPKS grades, and is paid to manufacturers and importers so farmers can buy at subsidised prices.
  • For farmers, the decision-critical figure is unchanged: the retail price of a 50 kg bag of DAP stays at Rs 1,350, the government said.

The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on Wednesday approved the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) rates for phosphatic and potassic (P&K) fertilisers for the Rabi 2026-27 season, with a tentative budget requirement of Rs 62,370.02 crore, according to the government's Cabinet release.

The outlay is Rs 24,417.73 crore more than the Rs 37,952.29 crore estimated for Rabi 2025-26, an increase of nearly 64%. The government said it reset the rates in view of recent trends in the international prices of fertilisers and inputs such as urea, DAP, MOP and sulphur.

The Rates

Under the approved NBS rates, the subsidy is fixed at Rs 94.21 per kg for nitrogen, Rs 66.11 per kg for phosphorus, Rs 2.38 per kg for potash and Rs 10.42 per kg for sulphur, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. The rates apply from October 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027 — the Rabi, or winter-sown, season that covers crops such as wheat, mustard and gram.

The subsidy covers 28 grades of P&K fertilisers, including di-ammonium phosphate (DAP) and NPKS grades. It does not go directly to farmers: it is paid to fertiliser manufacturers and importers at the approved rates, so that the fertilisers reach farmers at subsidised prices. The NBS scheme has governed P&K fertiliser subsidy since April 1, 2010.

What Farmers Will Pay

The price a farmer actually hands over for the most widely used P&K fertiliser is unchanged. Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw told reporters after the Cabinet meeting that the retail price of DAP would remain Rs 1,350 per 50 kg bag, despite rising global fertiliser prices.

Vaishnaw also said the country's fertiliser stocks stood at 235 lakh tonnes as of Wednesday, compared with 173 lakh tonnes in the corresponding period last year — the supply position the government is pointing to as it holds prices through the sowing season.

Why the Bill Rose

The Rs 62,370.02 crore figure is a tentative budget requirement for the six-month season, not final spending. Its size reflects the gap the subsidy has to bridge: when international prices of fertiliser inputs rise and the retail price to the farmer is held fixed, the difference lands on the government's subsidy bill. This Rabi season, that difference is about 64% larger than a year ago.
image_caption: A farmer broadcasts fertiliser by hand over a green field. The Cabinet has approved Rs 62,370 crore in P&K fertiliser subsidy for Rabi 2026-27 while holding the DAP bag price at Rs 1,350.
nri_angle: For diaspora readers with farming families in India, the held DAP price of Rs 1,350 per 50 kg bag is the figure that reaches the farm gate this Rabi season.
